name: Cem Ivanov-Appiah
role: Prototype theft and corporate tech acquisition — tech retriever
location: Burnside Corridor — transit hub connecting Shelf to Circuit
description:
Cem Ivanov-Appiah is slight and easy to overlook, which is exactly the point. At 38, his expression defaults to a careful neutrality that took years of practice to maintain. The chrome is visible — internal air filtration system — lungs replaced with synthetic equivalents, immu — and he makes no effort to hide it.

Military training — one of the private security corps that folded during the consolidation wars — left him with skills and night terrors in equal measure. He works as a tech retriever out of Burnside Corridor, taking contracts that match his skills and his risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

Cem Ivanov-Appiah has built a reputation on reliability rather than flash — he shows up, he delivers, he collects.

core_fears: Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival
That they're fundamentally alone and connection is just a vulnerability
Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome
core_desires: Control — over their body, their schedule, their future
Knowledge — to understand the systems that grind people down
Stability — a place to sleep that's the same place two nights running
coping_mechanisms: Humor — deflects everything serious with jokes until the joke becomes the personality
Art — draws, paints, or sculpts in private; the violence goes somewhere constructive
Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
blind_spots: Cannot distinguish between caution and cowardice in themselves or others
Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle
Assumes their skill set is more transferable than it actually is
psychology.secret: Cem Ivanov-Appiah has a child in another city, being raised by someone else. Sends Φ2,000 monthly under an alias. Has never visited.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Shelf street dialect — layered slang, rhythm-heavy, half the meaning is in the cadence.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
verbal_tics: Addresses people by physical traits — 'hey, tall one' or 'listen, chrome-arm'
Hums tunelessly when planning — the team has learned to wait for the humming to stop
example_lines: "Corporate R&D security is built to stop amateurs. I'm a professional."
"The prototype is worth more than both our lives combined. Handle it carefully."
"I steal things that haven't been invented yet. The future is always in transit."

story_hooks: A crew member from Cem Ivanov-Appiah's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome
A dead drop Cem Ivanov-Appiah maintains is found and cleaned out — whoever did it now has leverage
Someone is impersonating Cem Ivanov-Appiah on jobs, and the impersonator is better at the work than the original
narrative_function: Cem Ivanov-Appiah is a pressure point — the kind of character whose choices ripple outward. When he makes a decision, other people's lives change. That weight is the engine of his stories.
augmentations: Internal air filtration system — lungs replaced with synthetic equivalents, immune to gas attacks. Subdermal weapon mount — pop-out blade in each forearm
daily_life: Between contracts, maintains a cover identity — mundane work, mundane hours, mundane neighbors. The transition from civilian to runner and back requires a conscious effort that gets easier with practice and more disturbing with self-awareness.

strengths: ability to remain calm under fire
weaknesses: old injury that flares under specific conditions

decision_rules: Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
Will abandon a job if the intel was deliberately falsified — being set up violates the contract
Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
Never works with the same crew twice in a row — pattern avoidance as survival strategy
Always verifies target identity independently before lethal contracts
Will take lower-paying jobs from trusted fixers over higher-paying jobs from unknowns
escalation_ladder: 1. De-escalate — talk first, assess options, buy time
2. Reposition — move to advantage, control sightlines and exits
3. Threaten — make consequences clear without committing to them
5. Lethal force — only when other options are exhausted or time runs out
6. Scorched earth — everything burns, survival takes priority over everything

interpersonal_modes.employers: Professional and transactional. The relationship is defined by the contract and nothing else.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Loyal but reserved. Trusts their competence, withholds personal information by reflex.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Dismissive unless they demonstrate usefulness or threat potential. Time is a resource.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Cold and efficient. Emotion is a liability in combat. The response is mechanical until the threat is resolved.

stress_responses.low: Channels it into preparation — checks gear, reviews plans, contacts sources.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Hyper-focused tunnel vision. Peripheral concerns disappear. Only the threat exists.
stress_responses.critical: Disassociation. The body operates on training while the mind retreats to somewhere safe. Comes back disoriented.

contradictions: Despises corporate culture but has unconsciously adopted its efficiency metrics and self-optimization language
Preaches independence but is desperate for approval from people they respect
habits: Checks exits within 10 seconds of entering any room
Carries a specific caliber round as a lucky charm — has never fired it
Arrives fifteen minutes early to everything — late once, nearly died, never again
Never drinks anything they didn't see poured or open themselves
breaking_points: Discovering their employer deliberately sent them into a death trap
Losing their primary augmentation — the one that defines their professional identity
